name: pagination
purpose: Pagination controls for tables and lists, pixel-perfect to Figma, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): a three-region landmark — page-info text, navigation buttons (Previous / page numbers / overflow / Next), and a rows-per-page selector — wired by hand through slots, with the consumer owning the current page, total, and page-size state. **Data-driven mode**: pass `total` (and optionally `page` / `pageSize`) and the Pagination renders its own info text, Previous / windowed page numbers / overflow ellipsis / Next, and the rows-per-page selector, emitting `update:page` / `update:pageSize` so the consumer can bind state via `v-model`. This component owns markup, tokens, and a11y; the data engine is a small internal page-window calculation — **no external pagination library**. Pairs with the [`Table`](table.md) component.
useWhen: A list or table outside `table`'s own footer needs page navigation and a rows-per-page selector.
You know the item count — pass `total` and bind `v-model:page` / `v-model:page-size`; the component renders the info text, the windowed page numbers and the selector.
The page strip needs custom content (a different info line, extra controls) — compose `Pagination.Info`, `Pagination.Button` and `Pagination.PageSize` through the slots.
avoidWhen: The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table; it renders this pagination in its footer and wires it for you.
It is the previous / next pair at the end of a documentation page → use `doc-pagination`.
The content loads more as the reader scrolls or clicks "Load more" → use a `button` at the end of the list.
related: table` — renders a wired pagination in its footer when `paginated` is set.
doc-pagination` — previous / next links between documentation pages, not numbered pages of a list.
bestPractices: Prefer data-driven mode (`total` set); in composition mode the root emits nothing and you own every button's `selected` / `disabled` state and every click.
page` is 1-based. Changing the page size through the selector emits `update:pageSize` and resets the page to `1`.
Keep `page-size-options` aligned with what your data source accepts; the default is `[10, 25, 50, 100]`.
Tune `sibling-count` (default `1`) instead of hiding buttons — it controls how many numbers sit on each side of the current page before the overflow ellipsis.
Set `aria-label` when a page carries more than one pagination, so each navigation landmark has a distinct name.

props.name: total
props.doc: Total item count. When set, the Pagination runs in data-driven mode and renders its own controls.

props.name: pageSizeOptions
props.doc: Page-size options offered in the rows-per-page selector.

props.name: siblingCount
props.doc: Page numbers shown on each side of the current page before collapsing into an overflow ellipsis.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Pagination`).

events.name: update:page
events.notes: Current page changed in data-driven mode (Previous / Next / page number). Supports `v-model:page`.

events.name: update:pageSize
events.notes: Rows-per-page changed via the internal selector. Supports `v-model:page-size`.

slots.name: info
slots.notes: Left region: page-info text (typically PaginatorInfo). In data-driven mode, overrides the default "Showing X to Y of Z entries" text.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Center region: pagination navigation buttons (composition mode only — ignored in data-driven mode, where the buttons are rendered internally).

slots.name: controls
slots.notes: Right region: rows-per-page selector (PaginatorPageSize). In data-driven mode, overrides the internally-rendered selector.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
</script>

<template>
  <Pagination>
    <template #info>
      <Pagination.Info>Showing 1 to 10 of 20 entries</Pagination.Info>
    </template>

    <Pagination.Button
      kind="previous"
      aria-label="Previous page"
      disabled
    />
    <Pagination.Button
      kind="number"
      selected
      >1</Pagination.Button
    >
    <Pagination.Button kind="number">2</Pagination.Button>
    <Pagination.Button kind="number">3</Pagination.Button>
    <Pagination.Button kind="more" />
    <Pagination.Button
      kind="next"
      aria-label="Next page"
    />

    <template #controls>
      <Pagination.PageSize
        :model-value="10"
        :options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
      />
    </template>
  </Pagination>
</template>

examples.name: Buttons
DataDriven
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const page = ref(1)
  const pageSize = ref(10)
</script>

<template>
  <PaginationRoot
    v-model:page="page"
    v-model:page-size="pageSize"
    :total="200"
    :page-size-options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
    :sibling-count="1"
  />
</template>
